ko.title: [Retailing 101 #10] 치약을 사러 갔다가 87달러를 더 쓰고 나왔다면, 그건 매장 배치가 한 짓이다.

segments.src: > A store is not a warehouse with a cash register attached — it's a physical argument for buying more, written in aisles, sightlines, and shelf height.
segments.tr: > 매장은 계산대가 달린 창고가 아니다. 통로, 시야, 선반 높이로 쓰인 더 많이 사도록 하는 물리적 주장이다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Every store you walk into is the product of thousands of small decisions about **where things go**.
segments.tr: 매장마다 **물건을 어디에 놓을지**에 대한 수천 개의 작은 결정이 담겨 있다.

segments.src: Retailers call this work store operations and **visual merchandising** (often shortened to VMD, for visual merchandising and display).
segments.tr: 소매업자들은 이 작업을 점포 운영과 **비주얼 머천다이징**(시각적 상품 진열을 뜻하는 VMD로 줄임)이라고 부른다.

segments.src: It breaks into three moving parts.
segments.tr: 이는 세 가지 움직이는 부분으로 나뉜다.

segments.src: Layout — the skeleton.**
segments.tr: 매장 배치 — 골격.**

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:
segments.tr: 세 가지 기본 패턴이 미국 소매업의 대부분을 차지한다:

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **격자형**: 길게 나란한 통로. 식료품점, CVS, Home Depot. 효율적이고 제곱피트당 가장 많은 상품을 집어넣을 수 있으며 케첩을 찾기 쉽다. 하지만 산업적으로 느껴지고 쇼핑객들이 빠르게 지나가는 경향이 있다.

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **레이스트랙(루프)**: 매장 바닥을 한 바퀴 도는 메인 통로로, 부서를 지난다. 메이시스 층이나 이케아를 생각해보라. 지나가는 상품의 양을 최대화한다.

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **자유형**: 느슨하게 배열된 진열대, 정해진 경로 없음. 부티크, 애플 스토어, 세포라. 쇼핑을 장려하지만 공간을 낭비하므로 마진이 높을 때만 효과가 있다.

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: 고객 흐름 — 안무.**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: 소매업자들은 선반뿐 아니라 경로를 계획한다.

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 작동 원칙:

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **감압 존(decompression zone)**. 입구 안쪽 처음 5~15피트는 전환 영역이다. 사람들은 여전히 적응 중이다. 안내판을 읽고, 휴대폰을 집어넣고, 카트를 집는다. 거기 놓인 상품은 무시된다. 똑똑한 매장은 그곳을 상대적으로 열려 있게 둔다.

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **우측 표류(rightward drift)**. 사람들이 우측 도로에서 운전하는 시장에서, 매장에 들어오는 쇼핑객들은 우측으로 표류하는 경향이 있다. 이는 소매 관찰 연구(Paco Underhill의 *Why We Buy*가 대중화했음)에서 나온 널리 사용되는 계획 가정이지만, 고정된 법칙은 아니다. 매장, 입구 배치, 연구에 따라 다르다. 그래서 당신의 우측 바로 옆 벽은 흔히 신상품이나 시즌의 주요 상품으로 가득한 **파워 월(power wall)**이다.

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **목적지 상품은 멀리 둔다**. 우유, 계란, 의약품은 매장 뒤쪽에 있다. 당신은 그들이 필요하므로 걸을 것이다. 그 보행이 포인트다.

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **속도 제한 장치(speed bumps)**. 빠른 보행을 방해하고 당신을 쇼핑 모드로 늦추기 위해 배치된 테이블, 디스플레이, 엔드캡.

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **통로 폭이 생각보다 중요하다**. Underhill은 "엉덩이 문지르기 효과(butt-brush effect)"를 기록했다: 상품을 검토하는 동안 뒤에서 부딪히는 쇼핑객들은 그것을 포기하고 이동하는 경향이 있다. 별도로, 미국 접근성 규칙이 기준을 설정한다. 2010 ADA 표준에 따르면, 접근 가능한 경로는 일반적으로 최소 36인치의 명확한 폭이 필요하다. 하나의 추가 진열대를 밀어 넣으면 판매 문제이자 준수 문제가 될 수 있다.

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: 비주얼 머천다이징 — 설득 계층.**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: 이는 표현 자체다: 윈도우 디스플레이, 마네킹, 조명, 안내판, 색상 블로킹, 그리고 **플래노그램**(정확히 어느 제품이 어디에, 어느 방향으로, 얼마나 많은 면이 있는지를 지정하는 선반별 다이어그램).

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: 여기서 대체로 따르는 규칙은 친숙하다: "눈높이가 구매 높이"이다. 대략 4~5피트 위로, 가장 많은 관심을 받고 일반적으로 최고 판매 또는 최고 마진 상품을 받는 범위다.

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: 자체 브랜드 제품은 눈높이에 자주 앉아있는 반면 내셔널 브랜드는 위나 아래로 밀려난다.

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: 어린이용 시리얼은 낮게, 어린이 눈높이에 앉는다.

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: **엔드캡** — 통로 끝의 디스플레이 — 은 주요 영역이며, 식료품과 대량 소매에서 브랜드는 무역 촉진 기금을 통해 자주 비용을 지불한다.

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: **크로스 머천다이징**은 보완 제품을 함께 배치한다: 칩 옆의 살사, 장난감 옆의 배터리.

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: 이것은 더 이상 추측이 아니다.

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.
segments.tr: 매장은 이를 측정한다: 도어 카운터, Wi-Fi 및 카메라 기반 트래픽 분석, 체류 시간의 히트맵.

segments.src: The scoreboard metrics are simple enough to write in plain text:
segments.tr: 스코어보드 메트릭은 평문으로 쓰기에 충분할 정도로 간단하다:

segments.src: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area
segments.tr: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area

segments.src: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors
segments.tr: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors

segments.src: average transaction value = sales / transactions
segments.tr: average transaction value = sales / transactions

segments.src: Layout and VMD are levers on all three.
segments.tr: 매장 배치와 비주얼 머천다이징은 셋 모두의 레버다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활에서

segments.src: It's Sunday afternoon and you drive to Target for toothpaste.
segments.tr: 일요일 오후, 당신은 치약을 사기 위해 Target으로 운전해간다.

segments.src: Ten dollars, tops.
segments.tr: 10달러가 최대다.

segments.src: You walk in and the entrance is deliberately open — decompression zone.
segments.tr: 당신은 들어가고 입구는 의도적으로 열려 있다 — 감압 존.

segments.src: You veer right, because everyone does, and there's the seasonal display: back-to-school, or patio furniture, or Halloween in early September.
segments.tr: 당신은 우측으로 꺾인다. 모두가 그렇듯이. 거기에 시즈널 디스플레이가 있다: 개학 준비, 또는 파티오 가구, 또는 9월 초 할로윈.

segments.src: Just past it, Bullseye's Playground — the "dollar spot" — a low-fixture maze of $1 to $5 items positioned exactly where your guard is down and your basket is empty.
segments.tr: 바로 그 너머, Bullseye's Playground — "달러 스팟" — 당신의 경계가 내려가고 바구니가 비어있는 정확히 그곳에 배치된 $1~$5 상품의 저 진열대 미로.

segments.src: Two candles and a notebook: $12.
segments.tr: 양초 두 개와 노트북: $12.

segments.src: Toothpaste is in Health & Beauty, deep along the back wall.
segments.tr: 치약은 Health & Beauty에 있고, 뒷벽을 깊숙이 따라간다.

segments.src: Getting there means walking the racetrack past apparel and home goods.
segments.tr: 거기 도달하려면 의류와 홈 굿즈를 지나 레이스트랙을 따라 걷는 것을 의미한다.

segments.src: On the way you pass an endcap of coffee pods on promotion, so those go in ($15).
segments.tr: 도중에 홍보 중인 커피 포드의 엔드캡을 지나가므로 그것이 들어간다 ($15).

segments.src: In the toothpaste aisle itself, your brand at eye level runs $5.49; the store brand is right beside it, and the 89-cent travel size is down by your knees.
segments.tr: 치약 통로 자체에서, 눈높이의 당신 브랜드는 $5.49; 매장 브랜드는 바로 옆에 있고, 89센트 여행용 사이즈는 당신의 무릎 아래에 있다.

segments.src: Grocery is on the far side, so you swing through for milk — at the very back, naturally — and pass the chips, which sit next to a salsa display that isn't in the salsa aisle at all.
segments.tr: 식료품은 저편에 있으므로, 당신은 우유를 위해 휘돌아 간다. 물론 맨 뒤에. 그리고 칩을 지나간다. 칩은 살사 통로에 전혀 없는 살사 디스플레이 옆에 앉아있다.

segments.src: Cross-merchandising ($9).
segments.tr: 크로스 머천다이징 ($9).

segments.src: At checkout: gum, candy, phone chargers, a $6 magazine, and a cooler of drinks.
segments.tr: 체크아웃에서: 껌, 사탕, 휴대폰 충전기, $6 잡지, 음료 냉장고.

segments.src: Impulse zone.
segments.tr: 충동 존.

segments.src: Receipt: $87.34.
Toothpaste was $5.49 of it.
segments.tr: 그 중 치약은 $5.49였다.

segments.src: Nothing manipulative happened — no one lied to you, no one hid a price.
segments.tr: 조작적인 일은 일어나지 않았다. 아무도 당신에게 거짓말을 하지 않았고, 아무도 가격을 숨기지 않았다.

segments.src: You simply walked through a space engineered so that the highest number of appealing things crossed your field of vision while you were already in buying mode.
segments.tr: 당신은 단순히 당신이 이미 구매 모드에 있는 동안 매력적인 가장 많은 것들이 당신의 시야를 가로질러 지나가도록 설계된 공간을 걸었을 뿐이다.

segments.src: That's the entire job.
segments.tr: 그것이 전부다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. **Layout** (grid, racetrack, free-form) sets the skeleton — it determines how much merchandise a shopper physically walks past.
segments.tr: 1. **매장 배치**(격자형, 레이스트랙, 자유형)는 골격을 설정한다. 쇼핑객이 물리적으로 지나가는 상품의 양을 결정한다.

segments.src: 2. **Customer flow** is designed, not accidental: decompression zones, rightward drift, destination items at the back, and aisles wide enough to browse comfortably and legally.
segments.tr: 2. **고객 흐름**은 설계된 것이지, 우발적이 아니다: 감압 존, 우측 표류, 뒤쪽의 목적지 상품, 그리고 편안하고 합법적으로 쇼핑하기에 충분히 넓은 통로.

segments.src: 3. **VMD** — planograms, eye-level placement, endcaps, and cross-merchandising — converts that traffic into transactions, and it's measured in sales per square foot and conversion rate.
segments.tr: 3. **비주얼 머천다이징** — 플래노그램, 눈높이 배치, 엔드캡, 크로스 머천다이징 — 은 그 트래픽을 거래로 변환하며, 이는 제곱피트당 판매액과 전환율로 측정된다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자체 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** Why do grocery stores put milk and eggs at the back of the store?
segments.tr: **1.** 식료품점은 왜 우유와 계란을 매장 뒤에 두는가?

segments.src: - (A) Refrigeration equipment can only be installed along the back wall
segments.tr: - (A) 냉장 장비는 뒷벽을 따라서만 설치할 수 있다

segments.src: - (B) They're destination items, so making shoppers walk to them exposes them to more merchandise
segments.tr: - (B) 그들은 목적지 상품이므로 쇼핑객들이 그들을 위해 걷게 하면 더 많은 상품에 노출된다

segments.src: - (C) Health regulations require perishables to be kept away from entrances
segments.tr: - (C) 보건 규정은 부패하기 쉬운 상품을 입구로부터 멀리 유지하도록 요구한다

segments.src: - (D) It reduces theft of high-value goods
segments.tr: - (D) 고가 상품의 도난을 줄인다

segments.src: **2.** A boutique clothing store with high margins and a browsing-oriented clientele would most likely use which layout?
segments.tr: **2.** 높은 마진과 쇼핑 지향적 고객층을 가진 부티크 의류점은 어느 배치를 가장 가능성 높게 사용하겠는가?

segments.src: - (A) Grid
segments.tr: - (A) 격자형

segments.src: - (B) Racetrack
segments.tr: - (B) 레이스트랙

segments.src: - (C) Free-form
segments.tr: - (C) 자유형

segments.src: - (D) Warehouse rack
segments.tr: - (D) 창고 진열대

segments.src: **3.** O/X: The "decompression zone" is the area just inside a store's entrance, and it's considered prime real estate for high-margin displays.
segments.tr: **3.** O/X: "감압 존"은 매장 입구 바로 안쪽의 영역이며, 고마진 디스플레이의 주요 부동산으로 간주된다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Planogram**: A shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product goes where, how many facings it gets, and in what order.
segments.tr: - **플래노그램**: 정확히 어느 제품이 어디에 가는지, 얼마나 많은 면을 받는지, 어떤 순서로 가는지를 지정하는 선반별 다이어그램.

segments.src: - **Endcap**: The display fixture at the end of an aisle; high-visibility space often funded by brands through trade promotion.
segments.tr: - **엔드캡**: 통로 끝의 디스플레이 고정 장치; 무역 촉진을 통해 브랜드에 의해 자주 자금을 받는 높은 가시성 공간.

segments.src: - **Decompression zone**: The first several feet inside the entrance where shoppers are still adjusting and largely tune out merchandise.
segments.tr: - **감압 존**: 입구 안쪽 처음 여러 피트로, 쇼핑객들이 여전히 적응 중이고 상품을 대체로 무시하는 곳.

segments.src: - **Power wall**: The wall a shopper faces or drifts toward on entry — typically the right-hand wall — used for new arrivals or headline items.
segments.tr: - **파워 월**: 쇼핑객이 입장할 때 마주하거나 향해 표류하는 벽 — 일반적으로 오른쪽 벽 — 신상품이나 주요 항목에 사용됨.

segments.src: - **Sales per square foot**: Annual sales divided by selling area; the standard productivity yardstick for physical retail space.
segments.tr: - **제곱피트당 판매**: 판매 면적으로 나눈 연간 판매; 물리적 소매 공간의 표준 생산성 척도.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — (B)**.
Milk is a destination item: shoppers will cross the store for it regardless, so retailers use that walk to expose them to impulse categories.

zh.title: [零售学 101 #10] 你为了牙膏进门，结果花了 $87。这全是楼层设计的功劳。

segments.src: > A store is not a warehouse with a cash register attached — it's a physical argument for buying more, written in aisles, sightlines, and shelf height.
segments.tr: > 商店不是装了收银机的仓库——它是一个物理空间，用走道、视线和货架高度来论证你应该买更多。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Every store you walk into is the product of thousands of small decisions about **where things go**.
segments.tr: 你走进的每家商店都是数千个关于**商品摆放位置**的小决策的产物。

segments.src: Retailers call this work store operations and **visual merchandising** (often shortened to VMD, for visual merchandising and display).
segments.tr: 零售商称这项工作为门店运营和**视觉陈列**（通常简称为 VMD，即视觉陈列和展示）。

segments.src: It breaks into three moving parts.
segments.tr: 它分为三个主要部分。

segments.src: Layout — the skeleton.**
segments.tr: 楼层平面——骨架。**

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:
segments.tr: 三种基本模式涵盖了大多数美国零售：

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **网格布局**：长平行过道。杂货店、CVS、Home Depot 等。这种布局高效，能在每平方英尺内放最多产品，也便于顾客找到番茄酱。但它看起来很工业化，顾客往往会快速穿过。

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **环形走廊**：一条主过道围绕楼层循环，经过一个个部门。想想 Macy's 或 Ikea 的楼层。它能最大化你经过的商品数量。

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **自由式布局**：货架随意排列，没有固定路线。精品店、Apple Store、丝芙兰。这种布局鼓励浏览但浪费空间，只有当利润空间大时才值得。

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: 客户流动——舞蹈编排。**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: 零售商规划的是顾客路线，不仅仅是货架。

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: 几条行之有效的原则：

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **缓冲区**。进门后的前 5-15 英尺是过渡区。人们仍在适应——阅读标识、收起手机、拿购物车。放在那里的商品会被忽视。聪明的商店会让它保持相对开放。

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **向右漂移**。在靠右行驶的市场中，进入商店的顾客往往会向右漂移。这是零售观察研究中广泛使用的规划假设（Paco Underhill 的*《我们为什么买》*使其流行），但不是铁律——它因商店、入口位置和研究而异。这就是为什么你右边的墙通常是**主力墙**，陈列着新品或本季头号商品。

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **目标商品放在远处**。牛奶、鸡蛋和药房位于商店的后面。你需要它们，所以你会走过去。走的过程才是重点。

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **减速带**。放置的桌子、陈列架和货架端头用来打断快速行走，让你进入浏览模式。

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **过道宽度比你想的更重要**。Underhill 记录了"臀部碰撞效应"：从后面被碰撞的购物者在检查产品时往往会放弃它并继续走。另外，美国无障碍法规在这里设定了下限——根据 2010 年《美国残疾人法案》标准，无障碍通道通常需要至少 36 英寸的有效宽度。再塞一个货架既是销售问题，也是合规问题。

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: 视觉陈列——说服层。**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: 这就是呈现方式本身：橱窗展示、模特、照明、标识、色彩搭配和**商品陈列图**（逐架指定具体哪个产品放在哪里、面向哪个方向、占几个面宽）。

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: 这里的经验法则很熟悉："眼平线就是购买线"——大约离地 4 到 5 英尺，这个区域获得最多关注，通常放最畅销或利润最高的商品。

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: 自有品牌产品通常放在眼平线，而全国性品牌会被推到上面或下面。

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: 儿童麦片放得很低，在儿童的眼平线。

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: **货架端头**——过道尽头的陈列——是黄金位置，在杂货和大众零售中，品牌经常通过贸易推广资金为其付费。

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: **交叉销售**将互补商品放在一起：莎莎酱紧挨着薯片，电池紧挨着玩具。

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: 这一切都不再是猜测。

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.
segments.tr: 商店测量它：门计数器、Wi-Fi 和基于摄像头的流量分析，以及驻留时间热力图。

segments.src: The scoreboard metrics are simple enough to write in plain text:
segments.tr: 记分板指标很简单，可以用纯文本写出来：

segments.src: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area
segments.tr: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area

segments.src: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors
segments.tr: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors

segments.src: average transaction value = sales / transactions
segments.tr: average transaction value = sales / transactions

segments.src: Layout and VMD are levers on all three.
segments.tr: 楼层平面和视觉陈列是这三者的杠杆。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: It's Sunday afternoon and you drive to Target for toothpaste.
segments.tr: 周日下午，你开车去 Target 买牙膏。

segments.src: Ten dollars, tops.
segments.tr: 最多十块钱。

segments.src: You walk in and the entrance is deliberately open — decompression zone.
segments.tr: 你走进去，入口故意是开放的——缓冲区。

segments.src: You veer right, because everyone does, and there's the seasonal display: back-to-school, or patio furniture, or Halloween in early September.
segments.tr: 你向右转，因为每个人都这样做，那里有季节性展示：返校、户外家具或 9 月初的万圣节。

segments.src: Just past it, Bullseye's Playground — the "dollar spot" — a low-fixture maze of $1 to $5 items positioned exactly where your guard is down and your basket is empty.
segments.tr: 就过了它，靶心游乐场——"一元区"——一个由 1 美元到 5 美元商品组成的低货架迷宫，位置正好是你防御最低、篮子最空的地方。

segments.src: Two candles and a notebook: $12.
segments.tr: 两根蜡烛和一个笔记本：12 美元。

segments.src: Toothpaste is in Health & Beauty, deep along the back wall.
segments.tr: 牙膏在健康与美容区，深处沿着后墙。

segments.src: Getting there means walking the racetrack past apparel and home goods.
segments.tr: 到那里意味着沿着环形走廊走过服装和家居用品区。

segments.src: On the way you pass an endcap of coffee pods on promotion, so those go in ($15).
segments.tr: 路上你经过一个促销咖啡胶囊的货架端头，所以这些也放进去了（15 美元）。

segments.src: In the toothpaste aisle itself, your brand at eye level runs $5.49; the store brand is right beside it, and the 89-cent travel size is down by your knees.
segments.tr: 在牙膏过道本身，你的品牌在眼平线上卖 5.49 美元；店铺品牌就在它旁边，89 美分的旅行装在你膝盖下方。

segments.src: Grocery is on the far side, so you swing through for milk — at the very back, naturally — and pass the chips, which sit next to a salsa display that isn't in the salsa aisle at all.
segments.tr: 杂货在远处，所以你绕进去买牛奶——自然在最后面——并经过薯片，它们紧挨着一个根本不在莎莎酱过道的莎莎酱展示。

segments.src: Cross-merchandising ($9).
segments.tr: 交叉销售（9 美元）。

segments.src: At checkout: gum, candy, phone chargers, a $6 magazine, and a cooler of drinks.
segments.tr: 在结账处：口香糖、糖果、手机充电器、一本 6 美元的杂志和一冷柜饮料。

segments.src: Impulse zone.
segments.tr: 冲动购买区。

segments.src: Receipt: $87.34.
Toothpaste was $5.49 of it.
segments.tr: 牙膏占其中 5.49 美元。

segments.src: Nothing manipulative happened — no one lied to you, no one hid a price.
segments.tr: 没有发生任何操纵——没人对你撒谎，没人隐藏价格。

segments.src: You simply walked through a space engineered so that the highest number of appealing things crossed your field of vision while you were already in buying mode.
segments.tr: 你只是走过了一个精心设计的空间，使得最多数量的吸引人的东西在你已经处于购买模式时进入你的视野。

segments.src: That's the entire job.
segments.tr: 那就是整个工作。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. **Layout** (grid, racetrack, free-form) sets the skeleton — it determines how much merchandise a shopper physically walks past.
segments.tr: 1. **楼层平面**（网格、环形、自由式）设置骨架——它决定了购物者实际走过的商品数量。

segments.src: 2. **Customer flow** is designed, not accidental: decompression zones, rightward drift, destination items at the back, and aisles wide enough to browse comfortably and legally.
segments.tr: 2. **客户流动**是设计的，不是偶然的：缓冲区、向右漂移、后部目标商品和足够宽的过道，让浏览既舒适又合法。

segments.src: 3. **VMD** — planograms, eye-level placement, endcaps, and cross-merchandising — converts that traffic into transactions, and it's measured in sales per square foot and conversion rate.
segments.tr: 3. **视觉陈列**——商品陈列图、眼平线陈列、货架端头和交叉销售——将那个流量转换为交易，并按每平方英尺销售额和转化率来衡量。

segments.tr: ## ✅ 自我测试

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Planogram**: A shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product goes where, how many facings it gets, and in what order.
segments.tr: - **商品陈列图**：一个逐架的图表，具体说明哪个产品放在哪里、它占几个面宽，以及顺序。

segments.src: - **Endcap**: The display fixture at the end of an aisle; high-visibility space often funded by brands through trade promotion.
segments.tr: - **货架端头**：过道尽头的陈列货架；高可见度空间，通常由品牌通过贸易推广资金支持。

segments.src: - **Decompression zone**: The first several feet inside the entrance where shoppers are still adjusting and largely tune out merchandise.
segments.tr: - **缓冲区**：入口内的前几英尺，购物者仍在适应，大多不注意商品。

segments.src: - **Power wall**: The wall a shopper faces or drifts toward on entry — typically the right-hand wall — used for new arrivals or headline items.
segments.tr: - **主力墙**：购物者进入时面对或漂向的墙——通常是右墙——用于摆放新品或头号商品。

segments.src: - **Sales per square foot**: Annual sales divided by selling area; the standard productivity yardstick for physical retail space.
segments.tr: - **每平方英尺销售额**：年度销售额除以销售面积；物理零售空间的标准生产力衡量尺。

segments.tr: 牛奶是目标商品：购物者无论如何都会为了它穿过商店，所以零售商利用这段走动让他们接触冲动购买类别。

segments.src: (Refrigeration is placed on back walls partly for utility access, but the merchandising logic drives the layout choice.)
segments.tr: （制冷设备放在后墙部分是出于实用性考虑，但商品陈列逻辑驱动了布局选择。）

segments.src: **2 — (C)** Free-form.
It sacrifices space efficiency for a relaxed browsing feel, which only pencils out when gross margins are high enough to absorb the lost density.
segments.tr: 它牺牲了空间效率以获得轻松的浏览感觉，只有当利润空间足够大以吸收损失的密度时才划得来。

segments.src: **3 — X (False)**.

The first half is right, the second is backwards: merchandise in the decompression zone gets ignored because shoppers are still in transition, so retailers generally keep it open rather than filling it with displays.*

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **ग्रिड**: लंबे समानांतर गलियारे। किराना स्टोर, CVS, Home Depot। यह कुशल है, प्रति वर्ग फुट सबसे अधिक उत्पाद पैक करता है, और केचप खोजना आसान बनाता है। यह औद्योगिक महसूस होता है, और खरीदारों को यह तेजी से चलते हुए लगता है।

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **रेसट्रैक (लूप)**: एक मुख्य गलियारा जो विभाग के बाद विभाग को घेरता है। Macy's फ्लोर या Ikea के बारे में सोचें। यह आपके द्वारा चलाए जाने वाले माल की मात्रा को अधिकतम करता है।

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **फ्री-फॉर्म**: ढीले ढंग से व्यवस्थित फिक्सचर, कोई निश्चित पथ नहीं। Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora। यह ब्राउज़िंग को प्रोत्साहित करता है लेकिन स्थान बर्बाद करता है, इसलिए यह तभी सार्थक होता है जब मार्जिन अधिक हो।

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: ग्राहक प्रवाह — नृत्य नियोजन।**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: खुदरा विक्रेता पथ की योजना बनाते हैं, सिर्फ शेल्फ नहीं।

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: कुछ कार्यशील सिद्धांत:

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **डीकम्प्रेशन जोन।** दरवाजे के अंदर पहले 5-15 फीट एक संक्रमण क्षेत्र हैं। लोग अभी समायोजन कर रहे हैं — संकेत पढ़ रहे हैं, अपना फोन दूर रख रहे हैं, एक कार्ट पकड़ रहे हैं। वहां रखा माल अनदेखा हो जाता है। स्मार्ट स्टोर इसे अपेक्षाकृत खुला रखते हैं।

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **दाईं ओर की प्रवृत्ति।** उन बाजारों में जहां लोग दाईं ओर चलाते हैं, दुकान में प्रवेश करने वाले खरीदार दाईं ओर की ओर बहते हैं। यह खुदरा अवलोकन अनुसंधान (Paco Underhill के *Why We Buy* द्वारा लोकप्रिय) से एक व्यापक रूप से उपयोग की जाने वाली योजना धारणा है, लोहे का कानून नहीं — यह स्टोर, प्रवेश द्वार की स्थिति और अध्ययन के अनुसार भिन्न होता है। यही कारण है कि आपके दाईं ओर की दीवार अक्सर **शक्ति दीवार** होती है, नई आगमन या मौसम की हेडलाइन आइटम से भरी होती है।

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **गंतव्य आइटम दूर जाते हैं।** दूध, अंडे और फार्मेसी दुकान के पीछे बैठते हैं। आपको उनकी जरूरत है, तो आप चलेंगे। चलना बात है।

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **स्पीड बंप।** टेबल, डिस्प्ले और एंडकैप को तेजी से चलने को बाधित करने और आपको ब्राउज़िंग मोड में धीमा करने के लिए रखा जाता है।

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **गलियारे की चौड़ाई आपके विचार से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण है।** Underhill ने "बट-ब्रश प्रभाव" का दस्तावेज़ किया: जो खरीदार किसी उत्पाद की जांच करते समय पीछे से टकराते हैं, वे इसे छोड़ देते हैं और आगे बढ़ते हैं। अलग से, U.S. पहुंचनीयता नियम यहां एक मंजिल निर्धारित करते हैं — 2010 ADA मानकों के अनुसार, एक सुलभ मार्ग को आमतौर पर कम से कम 36 इंच स्पष्ट चौड़ाई की आवश्यकता होती है। एक और फिक्सचर को ठूंसना बिक्री समस्या और अनुपालन समस्या दोनों हो सकता है।

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: VMD — अनुनय परत।**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: यह प्रस्तुति स्वयं है: खिड़की के डिस्प्ले, मैनेक्विन, प्रकाश व्यवस्था, संकेत, रंग ब्लॉकिंग, और **planogram** (शेल्फ-दर-शेल्फ आरेख जो निर्दिष्ट करता है कि कौन सा उत्पाद कहां बैठता है, किस ओर का सामना करता है, कितने आमने-सामने चौड़े हैं)।

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: यहां अंगूठे के नियम परिचित हैं: "आंखों का स्तर खरीद स्तर है" — लगभग 4 से 5 फीट ऊपर, जो बैंड सबसे अधिक ध्यान आकर्षित करता है और आमतौर पर सबसे अधिक बिकने वाली या सर्वोच्च-मार्जिन आइटम।

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: निजी-लेबल उत्पाद अक्सर आंख के स्तर पर बैठते हैं जबकि राष्ट्रीय ब्रांड को ऊपर या नीचे धकेला जाता है।

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: बच्चों के सीरीज़ कम बैठते हैं, बच्चों की आंखों के स्तर पर।

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: **एंडकैप** — गलियारे के अंत में डिस्प्ले — प्रमुख क्षेत्र हैं, और किराने और जन खुदरा में, ब्रांड अक्सर व्यापार प्रचार फंड के माध्यम से उनके लिए भुगतान करते हैं।

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: **क्रॉस-मर्चेंडाइजिंग** पूरक को एक साथ रखता है: चिप्स के बगल में सल्सा, खिलौने के बगल में बैटरी।

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: यह सब अब अनुमान नहीं है।

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.
segments.tr: स्टोर इसे मापते हैं: दरवाजा काउंटर, Wi-Fi और कैमरा-आधारित ट्रैफिक विश्लेषण, और निवास समय के ताप मानचित्र।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. **Layout** (grid, racetrack, free-form) sets the skeleton — it determines how much merchandise a shopper physically walks past.
segments.tr: 1. **लेआउट** (ग्रिड, रेसट्रैक, फ्री-फॉर्म) कंकाल सेट करता है — यह निर्धारित करता है कि एक खरीदार कितने सामान से शारीरिक रूप से गुजरता है।

segments.src: 2. **Customer flow** is designed, not accidental: decompression zones, rightward drift, destination items at the back, and aisles wide enough to browse comfortably and legally.
segments.tr: 2. **ग्राहक प्रवाह** डिज़ाइन किया गया है, आकस्मिक नहीं: डीकम्प्रेशन जोन, दाईं ओर की प्रवृत्ति, पीछे में गंतव्य आइटम, और गलियारे आराम से और कानूनी रूप से ब्राउज़ करने के लिए काफी चौड़े।

segments.src: 3. **VMD** — planograms, eye-level placement, endcaps, and cross-merchandising — converts that traffic into transactions, and it's measured in sales per square foot and conversion rate.
segments.tr: 3. **VMD** — planograms, आंख स्तर की प्लेसमेंट, endcaps, और क्रॉस-मर्चेंडाइजिंग — उस ट्रैफिक को लेनदेन में परिवर्तित करता है, और इसे प्रति वर्ग फुट बिक्री और रूपांतरण दर में मापा जाता है।

segments.src: - (B) They're destination items, so making shoppers walk to them exposes them to more merchandise

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms

es.title: [Retailing 101 #10] Entraste por Pasta de Dientes y Saliste $87 Más Pobre. Fue lo que el Diseño de la Tienda Dijo.

segments.src: > A store is not a warehouse with a cash register attached — it's a physical argument for buying more, written in aisles, sightlines, and shelf height.
segments.tr: > Una tienda no es un almacén con una caja registradora adjunta — es un argumento físico para comprar más, escrito en pasillos, líneas de visión y altura de estantes.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Every store you walk into is the product of thousands of small decisions about **where things go**.
segments.tr: Cada tienda en la que entras es el producto de miles de pequeñas decisiones sobre **dónde van las cosas**.

segments.src: Retailers call this work store operations and **visual merchandising** (often shortened to VMD, for visual merchandising and display).
segments.tr: Los minoristas llaman a este trabajo operaciones de tienda y **visual merchandising** (a menudo acortado a VMD, por visual merchandising and display).

segments.src: It breaks into three moving parts.
segments.tr: Se divide en tres partes en movimiento.

segments.src: Layout — the skeleton.**
segments.tr: Diseño — el esqueleto.**

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:
segments.tr: Tres patrones básicos cubren la mayoría del retail estadounidense:

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **Cuadrícula**: pasillos largos y paralelos. Tiendas de abarrotes, CVS, Home Depot. Es eficiente, empaca la mayoría de productos por pie cuadrado, y facilita encontrar la salsa de tomate. También se siente industrial, y los compradores tienden a pasar por ella rápidamente.

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **Circuito (bucle)**: un pasillo principal que rodea el piso pasando departamento tras departamento. Piensa en un piso de Macy's o un Ikea. Maximiza la cantidad de mercancía por la que caminas.

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **Forma libre**: accesorios organizados libremente, sin camino fijo. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. Fomenta la exploración pero desperdicia espacio, por lo que solo es rentable cuando los márgenes son altos.

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: Flujo de clientes — la coreografía.**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: Los minoristas planean el camino, no solo los estantes.

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: Algunos principios de trabajo:

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **La zona de descompresión.** Los primeros 5–15 pies dentro de la puerta es un área de transición. Las personas todavía se están ajustando — leyendo señales, guardando su teléfono, agarrando un carrito. La mercancía colocada allí se ignora. Las tiendas inteligentes la dejan relativamente abierta.

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **La desviación hacia la derecha.** En mercados donde las personas conducen por la derecha, los compradores que entran en una tienda tienden a desviarse hacia la derecha. Es un supuesto de planificación ampliamente utilizado en la investigación de observación minorista (Paco Underhill popularizó *Why We Buy*), no una ley de hierro — varía según la tienda, la ubicación de la entrada y el estudio. Por eso, la pared inmediatamente a tu derecha a menudo es el **muro de poder**, cargado con nuevas llegadas o el artículo principal de la temporada.

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **Los artículos de destino van lejos.** La leche, los huevos y la farmacia están en el fondo de la tienda. Los necesitas, así que caminarás. El caminar es el punto.

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **Obstáculos de velocidad.** Mesas, exhibiciones y stands de fin de pasillo colocados para interrumpir una caminata rápida y ralentizarte en modo de exploración.

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **El ancho del pasillo importa más de lo que crees.** Underhill documentó el "efecto de roce": los compradores que son empujados desde atrás mientras examinan un producto tienden a abandonarlo y seguir adelante. Por separado, las reglas de accesibilidad de EE.UU. establecen un mínimo aquí — bajo los Estándares ADA de 2010, una ruta accesible generalmente necesita al menos 36 pulgadas de ancho libre. Meter un accesorio más puede ser tanto un problema de ventas como un problema de cumplimiento.

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: VMD — la capa de persuasión.**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: Esta es la presentación en sí: exhibiciones de ventana, maniquíes, iluminación, señalización, bloqueo de color, y el **planograma** (el diagrama de estante por estante que especifica exactamente qué producto se sienta dónde, frente a cuál dirección, cuántas caras de ancho).

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: Las reglas prácticas aquí son familiares: "el nivel del ojo es el nivel de compra" — aproximadamente 4 a 5 pies hacia arriba, la banda que recibe la mayoría de la atención y típicamente los artículos que se venden mejor o tienen los márgenes más altos.

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: Los productos de marca propia a menudo se sientan al nivel del ojo mientras que las marcas nacionales se empujan hacia arriba o hacia abajo.

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: Los cereales para niños se sientan bajo, al nivel del ojo de los niños.

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: **Stands de fin de pasillo** — la exhibición al final de un pasillo — es territorio privilegiado, y en el comercio minorista de abarrotes y masivo, las marcas frecuentemente pagan por ellos a través de fondos de promoción comercial.

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: **Comercialización cruzada** coloca complementos juntos: salsa al lado de los chips, baterías al lado de los juguetes.

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: Nada de esto es conjetura ya.

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.
segments.tr: Las tiendas lo miden: contadores de puertas, análisis de tráfico basado en Wi-Fi y cámaras, y mapas de calor del tiempo de permanencia.

segments.src: The scoreboard metrics are simple enough to write in plain text:
segments.tr: Las métricas del marcador son lo suficientemente simples para escribir en texto sin formato:

segments.src: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area
segments.tr: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area

segments.src: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors
segments.tr: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors

segments.src: average transaction value = sales / transactions
segments.tr: average transaction value = sales / transactions

segments.src: Layout and VMD are levers on all three.
segments.tr: El diseño y VMD son palancas en los tres.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: It's Sunday afternoon and you drive to Target for toothpaste.
segments.tr: Es domingo por la tarde y conduces a Target por pasta de dientes.

segments.src: Ten dollars, tops.
segments.tr: Diez dólares, máximo.

segments.src: You walk in and the entrance is deliberately open — decompression zone.
segments.tr: Entras y la entrada está deliberadamente abierta — zona de descompresión.

segments.src: You veer right, because everyone does, and there's the seasonal display: back-to-school, or patio furniture, or Halloween in early September.
segments.tr: Giras a la derecha, porque todos lo hacen, y está la exhibición estacional: regreso a la escuela, o muebles de patio, o Halloween a principios de septiembre.

segments.src: Just past it, Bullseye's Playground — the "dollar spot" — a low-fixture maze of $1 to $5 items positioned exactly where your guard is down and your basket is empty.
segments.tr: Justo después, Bullseye's Playground — el "dollar spot" — un laberinto de accesorios bajos de artículos de $1 a $5 posicionados exactamente donde tu guardia está bajo y tu canasta está vacía.

segments.src: Two candles and a notebook: $12.
segments.tr: Dos velas y un cuaderno: $12.

segments.src: Toothpaste is in Health & Beauty, deep along the back wall.
segments.tr: La pasta de dientes está en Salud y Belleza, profundamente a lo largo de la pared trasera.

segments.src: Getting there means walking the racetrack past apparel and home goods.
segments.tr: Llegar allí significa caminar el circuito pasando ropa y artículos del hogar.

segments.src: On the way you pass an endcap of coffee pods on promotion, so those go in ($15).
segments.tr: En el camino pasas un stand de fin de pasillo de cápsulas de café en promoción, así que esas entran ($15).

segments.src: In the toothpaste aisle itself, your brand at eye level runs $5.49; the store brand is right beside it, and the 89-cent travel size is down by your knees.
segments.tr: En el pasillo de pasta de dientes en sí, tu marca al nivel del ojo cuesta $5.49; la marca de la tienda está justo al lado, y el tamaño de viaje de 89 centavos está abajo a la altura de tus rodillas.

segments.src: Grocery is on the far side, so you swing through for milk — at the very back, naturally — and pass the chips, which sit next to a salsa display that isn't in the salsa aisle at all.
segments.tr: La tienda de abarrotes está al lado opuesto, así que pasas por leche — en el fondo, naturalmente — y pasas los chips, que se sientan al lado de una exhibición de salsa que no está en el pasillo de salsa en absoluto.

segments.src: Cross-merchandising ($9).
segments.tr: Comercialización cruzada ($9).

segments.src: At checkout: gum, candy, phone chargers, a $6 magazine, and a cooler of drinks.
segments.tr: En el pago: chicle, dulces, cargadores de teléfono, una revista de $6, y un enfriador de bebidas.

segments.src: Impulse zone.
segments.tr: Zona de impulso.

segments.src: Receipt: $87.34.
segments.tr: Recibo: $87.34.

segments.src: Toothpaste was $5.49 of it.
segments.tr: La pasta de dientes fue $5.49 de eso.

segments.src: Nothing manipulative happened — no one lied to you, no one hid a price.
segments.tr: Nada manipulador sucedió — nadie te mintió, nadie ocultó un precio.

segments.src: You simply walked through a space engineered so that the highest number of appealing things crossed your field of vision while you were already in buying mode.
segments.tr: Simplemente caminaste a través de un espacio diseñado de modo que el mayor número de cosas atractivas cruzaran tu campo de visión mientras ya estabas en modo de compra.

segments.src: That's the entire job.
segments.tr: Ese es el trabajo completo.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de Tres Líneas

segments.src: 1. **Layout** (grid, racetrack, free-form) sets the skeleton — it determines how much merchandise a shopper physically walks past.
segments.tr: 1. **Diseño** (cuadrícula, circuito, forma libre) establece el esqueleto — determina cuánta mercancía camina físicamente un comprador.

segments.src: 2. **Customer flow** is designed, not accidental: decompression zones, rightward drift, destination items at the back, and aisles wide enough to browse comfortably and legally.
segments.tr: 2. **Flujo de clientes** está diseñado, no es accidental: zonas de descompresión, desviación hacia la derecha, artículos de destino en la parte posterior, y pasillos lo suficientemente amplios para explorar cómodamente y legalmente.

segments.src: 3. **VMD** — planograms, eye-level placement, endcaps, and cross-merchandising — converts that traffic into transactions, and it's measured in sales per square foot and conversion rate.
segments.tr: 3. **VMD** — planogramas, colocación al nivel del ojo, stands de fin de pasillo, y comercialización cruzada — convierte ese tráfico en transacciones, y se mide en ventas por pie cuadrado y tasa de conversión.

segments.src: It breaks into three moving parts.
segments.tr: ينقسم إلى ثلاثة أجزاء متحركة.

segments.src: Layout — the skeleton.**
segments.tr: التخطيط — الهيكل العظمي.**

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:
segments.tr: ثلاثة أنماط أساسية تغطي معظم التجزئة الأمريكية:

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **Grid**: ممرات طويلة متوازية. متاجر البقالة، CVS، Home Depot. إنها فعالة، وتعبئ أكثر المنتجات لكل قدم مربع، وتجعل من السهل العثور على الكاتشب. تشعر أيضاً بطابع صناعي، والمتسوقون يميلون إلى التحرك عبرها بسرعة.

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **Racetrack (loop)**: ممر رئيسي يدور حول الأرضية بجانب قسم تلو الآخر. فكر في طابق Macy's أو Ikea. يعظم كمية البضائع التي تمر بها.

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **Free-form**: التركيبات مرتبة بشكل فضفاض، بدون مسار ثابت. المحلات الفاخرة، متاجر Apple، Sephora. يشجع التصفح لكن يهدر المساحة، لذا فإنه يستحق فقط عندما تكون الهوامش عالية.

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: تدفق العملاء — الرقصة.**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: يخطط تجار التجزئة المسار، ليس فقط الأرفف.

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: بعض المبادئ العاملة:

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **منطقة فك الضغط.** أول 5–15 قدماً داخل الباب هي منطقة انتقالية. الناس لا يزالون يتكيفون — يقرؤون اللافتات، يضعون هواتفهم بعيداً، يلتقطون عربة. البضائع الموضوعة هناك يتم تجاهلها. المتاجر الذكية تتركها مفتوحة نسبياً.

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **الانجراف نحو اليمين.** في الأسواق حيث يقود الناس على اليمين، يميل المتسوقون الذين يدخلون المتجر إلى الانجراف لليمين. إنه افتراض تخطيط مستخدم على نطاق واسع من أبحاث المراقبة بالتجزئة (كتاب Paco Underhill *لماذا نشتري* روج له)، وليس قانوناً حديدياً — يختلف حسب المتجر وموقع المدخل والدراسة. وهذا هو السبب في أن الجدار الموجود مباشرة على يمينك غالباً ما يكون **جدار القوة**، محمل بالعروض الجديدة أو السلعة الرئيسية للموسم.

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **السلع المقصودة تذهب بعيداً.** الحليب والبيض والصيدلية توجد في مؤخرة المتجر. تحتاجهم، لذا ستمشي. المشي هو الهدف.

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **مطبات السرعة.** الجداول والعروض والعروض النهائية الموضوعة لقطع المشي السريع وإبطاء وضعك في وضع التصفح.

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **عرض الممر مهم أكثر مما تتخيل.** وثق Underhill "تأثير فرشاة المؤخرة": المتسوقون الذين يصطدمون من الخلف أثناء فحص المنتج يميلون إلى التخلي عنه والمضي قدماً. بشكل منفصل، تحدد قواعس إمكانية الوصول الأمريكية حد أدنى هنا — بموجب معايير ADA 2010، يحتاج المسار الذي يمكن الوصول إليه بشكل عام إلى عرض واضح لا يقل عن 36 بوصة. يمكن أن يكون حشر تركيبة إضافية واحدة مشكلة في المبيعات ومشكلة امتثال.

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: العرض البصري — طبقة الإقناع.**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: هذا هو العرض نفسه: عروض النوافذ، والدمى، والإضاءة، واللافتات، وحجب الألوان، و **planogram** (الرسم البياني الذي يحدد بالضبط أي منتج يجلس أين، مواجهة بأي اتجاه، كم عرض الوجوه).

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: القواعد الأساسية هنا مألوفة: "مستوى العين هو مستوى الشراء" — تقريباً من 4 إلى 5 أقدام، النطاق الذي يحصل على أكثر الاهتمام وعادة ما يكون أفضل البيع أو السلع ذات أعلى هامش.

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: تجلس المنتجات الخاصة بالعلامة التجارية الخاصة غالباً على مستوى العين بينما يتم دفع العلامات الوطنية لأعلى أو لأسفل.

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: حبوب الأطفال تجلس منخفضة، عند مستوى عين الطفل.

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: **Endcaps** — العرض في نهاية الممر — هي أرض أولية، وفي متاجر البقالة والتجزئة الجماعية، تدفع العلامات التجارية مقابلها بشكل متكرر من خلال أموال العروض الترويجية التجارية.

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: **البيع المتقاطع** يضع المتممات معاً: الصلصة بجانب الرقائق، البطاريات بجانب الألعاب.

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: لا شيء من هذا حدس بعد الآن.

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.
segments.tr: المتاجر تقيسها: عدادات الأبواب، وتحليلات حركة المرور القائمة على Wi-Fi والكاميرا، وخرائط الحرارة لوقت الإقامة.

segments.tr: مقاييس لوحة النتائج بسيطة بما يكفي للكتابة بنص عادي:

segments.src: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area
segments.tr: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area

segments.src: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors
segments.tr: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors

segments.src: average transaction value = sales / transactions
segments.tr: average transaction value = sales / transactions

segments.src: Layout and VMD are levers on all three.
segments.tr: التخطيط والعرض البصري هما رافعات على جميع الثلاثة.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: It's Sunday afternoon and you drive to Target for toothpaste.
segments.tr: إنها بعد ظهر يوم الأحد وتذهب بالسيارة إلى Target لشراء معجون أسنان.

segments.src: Ten dollars, tops.
segments.tr: عشرة دولارات، كحد أقصى.

segments.src: You walk in and the entrance is deliberately open — decompression zone.
segments.tr: تدخل والمدخل مفتوح عن قصد — منطقة فك الضغط.

segments.src: You veer right, because everyone does, and there's the seasonal display: back-to-school, or patio furniture, or Halloween in early September.
segments.tr: تنحني لليمين، لأن الجميع يفعل ذلك، وهناك العرض الموسمي: العودة إلى المدرسة، أو أثاث الفناء، أو هالوين في أوائل سبتمبر.

segments.src: Just past it, Bullseye's Playground — the "dollar spot" — a low-fixture maze of $1 to $5 items positioned exactly where your guard is down and your basket is empty.
segments.tr: بعده مباشرة، ملعب Bullseye — "منطقة الدولار" — متاهة تركيبات منخفضة من عناصر بقيمة 1 إلى 5 دولارات موضوعة بالضبط حيث تكون حراستك منخفضة وسلتك فارغة.

segments.src: Two candles and a notebook: $12.
segments.tr: شمعتان ودفتر ملاحظات: 12 دولاراً.

segments.src: Toothpaste is in Health & Beauty, deep along the back wall.
segments.tr: معجون الأسنان موجود في Health & Beauty، عميق على طول الجدار الخلفي.

segments.src: Getting there means walking the racetrack past apparel and home goods.
segments.tr: الوصول إلى هناك يعني المشي على مضمار السباق بجانب الملابس والسلع المنزلية.

segments.src: On the way you pass an endcap of coffee pods on promotion, so those go in ($15).
segments.tr: في الطريق، تمر بجانب عرض نهائي لكبسولات القهوة قيد الترويج، لذا تدخل تلك ($15).

segments.src: In the toothpaste aisle itself, your brand at eye level runs $5.49; the store brand is right beside it, and the 89-cent travel size is down by your knees.
segments.tr: في ممر معجون الأسنان نفسه، علامتك التجارية عند مستوى العين تكلف 5.49 دولاراً؛ علامة المتجر موجودة بجانبها مباشرة، وحجم السفر بـ 89 سنتاً أسفل ركبتيك.

segments.src: Grocery is on the far side, so you swing through for milk — at the very back, naturally — and pass the chips, which sit next to a salsa display that isn't in the salsa aisle at all.
segments.tr: البقالة على الجانب الآخر، لذا تتأرجح للحصول على الحليب — في الجزء الخلفي تماماً، بالطبع — وتمر بجانب الرقائق، التي تجلس بجانب عرض صلصة ليس في ممر الصلصة على الإطلاق.

segments.src: Cross-merchandising ($9).
segments.tr: البيع المتقاطع ($9).

segments.src: At checkout: gum, candy, phone chargers, a $6 magazine, and a cooler of drinks.
segments.tr: عند الخروج: العلكة، والحلويات، ومشاحن الهواتف، مجلة بـ 6 دولارات، ومبرد المشروبات.

segments.src: Impulse zone.
segments.tr: منطقة الاندفاع.

segments.src: Receipt: $87.34.
segments.tr: الإيصال: 87.34 دولاراً.

segments.src: Toothpaste was $5.49 of it.
segments.tr: معجون الأسنان كان 5.49 دولاراً منها.

segments.src: Nothing manipulative happened — no one lied to you, no one hid a price.
segments.tr: لم يحدث شيء متلاعب به — لم يكذب أحد عليك، لم يخفِ أحد السعر.

segments.src: You simply walked through a space engineered so that the highest number of appealing things crossed your field of vision while you were already in buying mode.
segments.tr: لقد مشيت ببساطة عبر مساحة تم تصميمها بحيث يعبر أكبر عدد من الأشياء الجذابة حقل رؤيتك بينما كنت بالفعل في وضع الشراء.

segments.src: That's the entire job.
segments.tr: هذه هي الوظيفة برمتها.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. **Layout** (grid, racetrack, free-form) sets the skeleton — it determines how much merchandise a shopper physically walks past.
segments.tr: 1. **التخطيط** (الشبكة، مضمار السباق، الشكل الحر) يحدد الهيكل العظمي — يحدد كمية البضائع التي يمر بها المتسوق جسدياً.

segments.src: 2. **Customer flow** is designed, not accidental: decompression zones, rightward drift, destination items at the back, and aisles wide enough to browse comfortably and legally.
segments.tr: 2. **تدفق العملاء** مصمم، وليس بالصدفة: مناطق فك الضغط، والانجراف نحو اليمين، والسلع المقصودة في الخلف، والممرات واسعة بما يكفي للتصفح براحة وقانونياً.

segments.src: 3. **VMD** — planograms, eye-level placement, endcaps, and cross-merchandising — converts that traffic into transactions, and it's measured in sales per square foot and conversion rate.
segments.tr: 3. **العرض البصري** — planograms، والعرض على مستوى العين، والعروض النهائية، والبيع المتقاطع — يحول حركة المرور تلك إلى معاملات، ويتم قياسها بالمبيعات لكل قدم مربع ومعدل التحويل.

segments.tr: ## 📚 شروط اليوم

segments.src: - **Planogram**: A shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product goes where, how many facings it gets, and in what order.
segments.tr: - **Planogram**: رسم بياني من رف إلى رف يحدد بالضبط أي منتج يذهب أين، وكم عدد الوجوه التي يحصل عليها، وبأي ترتيب.

segments.src: - **Endcap**: The display fixture at the end of an aisle; high-visibility space often funded by brands through trade promotion.
segments.tr: - **Endcap**: تركيبة العرض في نهاية الممر؛ مساحة عالية الرؤية يتم تمويلها في كثير من الأحيان من قبل العلامات التجارية من خلال الترويج التجاري.

segments.src: - **Decompression zone**: The first several feet inside the entrance where shoppers are still adjusting and largely tune out merchandise.
segments.tr: - **منطقة فك الضغط**: أول عدة أقدام داخل المدخل حيث لا يزال المتسوقون يتكيفون وغالباً ما يتجاهلون البضائع.

segments.src: - **Power wall**: The wall a shopper faces or drifts toward on entry — typically the right-hand wall — used for new arrivals or headline items.

segments.src: - **Sales per square foot**: Annual sales divided by selling area; the standard productivity yardstick for physical retail space.

segments.src: > A store is not a warehouse with a cash register attached — it's a physical argument for buying more, written in aisles, sightlines, and shelf height.
segments.tr: > Un magasin n'est pas un entrepôt avec une caisse enregistreuse — c'est un argument physique pour acheter davantage, écrit dans les allées, les lignes de vue et la hauteur des rayons.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le Concept d'Aujourd'hui

segments.src: Every store you walk into is the product of thousands of small decisions about **where things go**.
segments.tr: Chaque magasin dans lequel vous entrez est le produit de milliers de petites décisions concernant **où placer les choses**.

segments.src: Retailers call this work store operations and **visual merchandising** (often shortened to VMD, for visual merchandising and display).
segments.tr: Les détaillants appellent ce travail exploitation de magasin et **merchandisage visuel** (souvent abrégé en VMD, pour merchandisage visuel et présentation).

segments.src: It breaks into three moving parts.
segments.tr: Il se divise en trois parties en mouvement.

segments.src: Layout — the skeleton.**
segments.tr: Disposition — le squelette.**

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:
segments.tr: Trois modèles de base couvrent la plupart du commerce de détail américain :

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **Grille** : allées parallèles longues. Épiceries, CVS, Home Depot. C'est efficace, entasse le plus de produits par pied carré et facilite la localisation du ketchup. Cela semble aussi industriel, et les clients ont tendance à le traverser rapidement.

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **Piste de course (boucle)** : une allée principale qui fait le tour du sol en passant d'un département à l'autre. Pensez à un étage de Macy's ou d'Ikea. Cela maximise la quantité de marchandises que vous dépassez.

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **Libre** : accessoires arrangés librement, pas de chemin fixe. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. Cela encourage la navigation mais gaspille l'espace, donc cela ne s'avère rentable que lorsque les marges sont élevées.

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: Flux de clients — la chorégraphie.**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: Les détaillants planifient le chemin, pas seulement les rayons.

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: Quelques principes de fonctionnement :

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **La zone de décompression.** Les premiers 5–15 pieds à l'intérieur de la porte constituent une zone de transition. Les gens s'adaptent encore — lisant les panneaux, rangeant leur téléphone, saisissant un panier. Les marchandises placées là-bas sont ignorées. Les magasins intelligents la laissent relativement ouverte.

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **La dérive vers la droite.** Sur les marchés où les gens conduisent à droite, les acheteurs entrant dans un magasin ont tendance à dériver vers la droite. C'est une hypothèse de planification largement utilisée à partir de la recherche sur l'observation du commerce de détail (le *Why We Buy* de Paco Underhill l'a popularisée), pas une loi de fer — elle varie selon le magasin, le placement de l'entrée et l'étude. C'est pourquoi le mur immédiatement à votre droite est souvent le **mur de puissance**, chargé des nouvelles arrivées ou de l'article vedette de la saison.

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **Les articles de destination s'éloignent.** Le lait, les œufs et la pharmacie se trouvent à l'arrière du magasin. Vous en avez besoin, donc vous marcherez. La marche est le point.

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **Ralentisseurs.** Tables, présentoirs et bouts de rayons placés pour interrompre une marche rapide et vous ralentir en mode navigation.

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **La largeur de l'allée compte plus que vous ne le pensez.** Underhill a documenté l'« effet de frôlement des fesses » : les acheteurs qui se font heurter par derrière en examinant un produit ont tendance à l'abandonner et à passer. Séparément, les règles d'accessibilité américaines fixent un plancher ici — selon les normes ADA de 2010, une route accessible a généralement besoin d'au moins 36 pouces de largeur libre. Entasser un accessoire supplémentaire peut être à la fois un problème de ventes et un problème de conformité.

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: VMD — la couche de persuasion.**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: C'est la présentation elle-même : vitrines, mannequins, éclairage, panneaux, blocage des couleurs et le **planogramme** (le diagramme étagère par étagère spécifiant exactement quel produit se trouve où, face à quel endroit, combien de façades de large).

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: Les règles empiriques ici sont familières : « le niveau des yeux est le niveau d'achat » — approximativement 4 à 5 pieds, la bande qui reçoit le plus d'attention et généralement les articles les plus vendus ou à plus forte marge.

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: Les produits de marque privée se situent souvent au niveau des yeux tandis que les grandes marques sont poussées vers le haut ou vers le bas.

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: Les céréales pour enfants sont placées bas, au niveau des yeux des enfants.

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: Les **bouts de rayons** — l'affichage au bout d'une allée — sont un territoire de choix, et dans l'épicerie et la vente au détail de masse, les marques les payent fréquemment par des fonds de promotion commerciale.

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: Le **marchandisage croisé** place les compléments ensemble : salsa à côté des chips, piles à côté des jouets.

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: Rien de tout cela n'est plus de la supposition.

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en Trois Lignes

segments.src: 1. **Layout** (grid, racetrack, free-form) sets the skeleton — it determines how much merchandise a shopper physically walks past.
segments.tr: 1. **La disposition** (grille, piste de course, libre) établit le squelette — elle détermine la quantité de marchandises qu'un acheteur traverse physiquement.

segments.src: 2. **Customer flow** is designed, not accidental: decompression zones, rightward drift, destination items at the back, and aisles wide enough to browse comfortably and legally.
segments.tr: 2. **Le flux de clients** est conçu, non accidentel : zones de décompression, dérive vers la droite, articles de destination à l'arrière, et allées suffisamment larges pour naviguer confortablement et légalement.

segments.src: 3. **VMD** — planograms, eye-level placement, endcaps, and cross-merchandising — converts that traffic into transactions, and it's measured in sales per square foot and conversion rate.
segments.tr: 3. **VMD** — planogrammes, placement au niveau des yeux, bouts de rayons et marchandisage croisé — convertit ce trafic en transactions, et il est mesuré en ventes par pied carré et taux de conversion.

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.

in.title: [Retailing 101 #10] Anda Masuk untuk Pasta Gigi dan Pergi $87 Lebih Miskin. Itu Rencana Tata Letak yang Berbicara.

segments.src: > A store is not a warehouse with a cash register attached — it's a physical argument for buying more, written in aisles, sightlines, and shelf height.
segments.tr: > Sebuah toko bukan gudang dengan mesin kasir yang melekat — ini adalah argumen fisik untuk membeli lebih banyak, yang ditulis dalam lorong, garis pandang, dan tinggi rak.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Every store you walk into is the product of thousands of small decisions about **where things go**.
segments.tr: Setiap toko yang Anda masuki adalah produk dari ribuan keputusan kecil tentang **di mana barang-barang ditempatkan**.

segments.src: Retailers call this work store operations and **visual merchandising** (often shortened to VMD, for visual merchandising and display).
segments.tr: Pengecer menyebut pekerjaan ini operasi toko dan **visual merchandising** (sering disingkat menjadi VMD, untuk visual merchandising dan display).

segments.src: It breaks into three moving parts.
segments.tr: Ini terbagi menjadi tiga bagian yang bergerak.

segments.src: Layout — the skeleton.**
segments.tr: Tata letak — kerangka kerja.**

segments.src: Three basic patterns cover most of American retail:
segments.tr: Tiga pola dasar mencakup sebagian besar ritel Amerika:

segments.src: - **Grid**: long parallel aisles. Grocery stores, CVS, Home Depot. It's efficient, packs the most product per square foot, and makes it easy to find the ketchup. It also feels industrial, and shoppers tend to move through it briskly.
segments.tr: - **Grid**: lorong-lorong paralel yang panjang. Toko bahan makanan, CVS, Home Depot. Ini efisien, mengemas produk paling banyak per kaki persegi, dan memudahkan menemukan saus tomat. Ini juga terasa industri, dan pembeli cenderung bergerak melaluinya dengan cepat.

segments.src: - **Racetrack (loop)**: a main aisle that circles the floor past department after department. Think a Macy's floor or an Ikea. It maximizes the amount of merchandise you walk past.
segments.tr: - **Racetrack (loop)**: lorong utama yang melingkari lantai melewati departemen demi departemen. Pikirkan lantai Macy's atau Ikea. Ini memaksimalkan jumlah barang dagangan yang Anda lewati.

segments.src: - **Free-form**: fixtures arranged loosely, no fixed path. Boutiques, Apple Stores, Sephora. It encourages browsing but wastes space, so it only pays off when margins are high.
segments.tr: - **Bebas bentuk**: perlengkapan diatur secara longgar, tidak ada jalur tetap. Butik, Toko Apple, Sephora. Ini mendorong penjelajahan tetapi membuang ruang, jadi hanya menguntungkan ketika margin tinggi.

segments.src: Customer flow — the choreography.**
segments.tr: Alur pelanggan — koreografi.**

segments.src: Retailers plan the path, not just the shelves.
segments.tr: Pengecer merencanakan jalur, bukan hanya rak-rak.

segments.src: A few working principles:
segments.tr: Beberapa prinsip kerja:

segments.src: - **The decompression zone.** The first 5–15 feet inside the door is a transition area. People are still adjusting — reading signage, putting away their phone, grabbing a cart. Merchandise placed there gets ignored. Smart stores leave it relatively open.
segments.tr: - **Zona dekompresi.** 5–15 kaki pertama di dalam pintu adalah area transisi. Orang-orang masih menyesuaikan — membaca tanda, menyimpan ponsel mereka, mengambil keranjang. Barang dagangan yang ditempatkan di sana diabaikan. Toko pintar membiarkannya tetap terbuka.

segments.src: - **The rightward drift.** In markets where people drive on the right, shoppers entering a store tend to drift right. It's a widely used planning assumption from retail observation research (Paco Underhill's *Why We Buy* popularized it), not an iron law — it varies by store, entrance placement, and study. Which is why the wall immediately to your right is often the **power wall**, loaded with new arrivals or the season's headline item.
segments.tr: - **Hanyut ke kanan.** Di pasar di mana orang berkendara di sebelah kanan, pembeli yang memasuki toko cenderung hanyut ke kanan. Ini adalah asumsi perencanaan yang banyak digunakan dari penelitian observasi ritel (buku *Why We Buy* karya Paco Underhill mempopulerkannya), bukan hukum besi — ini bervariasi menurut toko, penempatan pintu masuk, dan penelitian. Inilah mengapa dinding segera di sebelah kanan Anda sering kali adalah **dinding kekuatan**, penuh dengan kedatangan baru atau item tajuk berita musim ini.

segments.src: - **Destination items go far away.** Milk, eggs, and pharmacy sit at the back of the store. You need them, so you'll walk. The walk is the point.
segments.tr: - **Item tujuan pergi jauh.** Susu, telur, dan apotek berada di belakang toko. Anda membutuhkannya, jadi Anda akan berjalan. Perjalanannya adalah maksudnya.

segments.src: - **Speed bumps.** Tables, displays, and endcaps placed to interrupt a fast walk and slow you into browsing mode.
segments.tr: - **Polisi tidur.** Meja, display, dan endcap ditempatkan untuk mengganggu jalan yang cepat dan memperlambat Anda ke mode penjelajahan.

segments.src: - **Aisle width matters more than you'd think.** Underhill documented the "butt-brush effect": shoppers who get bumped from behind while examining a product tend to abandon it and move on. Separately, U.S. accessibility rules set a floor here — under the 2010 ADA Standards, an accessible route generally needs at least 36 inches of clear width. Cramming in one more fixture can be both a sales problem and a compliance problem.
segments.tr: - **Lebar lorong penting lebih dari yang Anda pikirkan.** Underhill mendokumentasikan "efek sapuan bokong": pembeli yang terdorong dari belakang saat memeriksa produk cenderung meninggalkannya dan melanjutkan. Secara terpisah, aturan aksesibilitas AS menetapkan lantai di sini — menurut Standar ADA 2010, rute yang dapat diakses umumnya memerlukan setidaknya 36 inci lebar bersih. Menyumbat satu perlengkapan lagi dapat menjadi masalah penjualan dan masalah kepatuhan.

segments.src: VMD — the persuasion layer.**
segments.tr: VMD — lapisan persuasi.**

segments.src: This is the presentation itself: window displays, mannequins, lighting, signage, color blocking, and the **planogram** (the shelf-by-shelf diagram specifying exactly which product sits where, facing which way, how many facings wide).
segments.tr: Ini adalah presentasi itu sendiri: display jendela, manekin, pencahayaan, signage, pemblokiran warna, dan **planogram** (diagram rak demi rak yang menentukan dengan tepat produk mana yang berada di mana, menghadap ke arah mana, berapa banyak fasing yang lebar).

segments.src: The rules of thumb here are familiar: "eye level is buy level" — roughly 4 to 5 feet up, the band that gets the most attention and typically the best-selling or highest-margin items.
segments.tr: Aturan praktis di sini akrab: "tingkat mata adalah tingkat beli" — kira-kira 4 hingga 5 kaki ke atas, pita yang mendapat perhatian paling banyak dan biasanya item terlaris atau margin tertinggi.

segments.src: Private-label products often sit at eye level while national brands get pushed up or down.
segments.tr: Produk label pribadi sering duduk di tingkat mata sementara merek nasional didorong ke atas atau ke bawah.

segments.src: Kids' cereal sits low, at kid eye level.
segments.tr: Sereal anak-anak duduk rendah, di tingkat mata anak.

segments.src: **Endcaps** — the display at the end of an aisle — are prime territory, and in grocery and mass retail, brands frequently pay for them through trade promotion funds.
segments.tr: **Endcap** — display di ujung lorong — adalah wilayah utama, dan dalam ritel bahan makanan dan massal, merek sering membayar untuk mereka melalui dana promosi perdagangan.

segments.src: **Cross-merchandising** places complements together: salsa next to the chips, batteries next to the toys.
segments.tr: **Cross-merchandising** menempatkan pelengkap bersama: salsa di sebelah keripik, baterai di sebelah mainan.

segments.src: None of this is guesswork anymore.
segments.tr: Tidak ada lagi tebakan-tebakan.

segments.src: Stores measure it: door counters, Wi-Fi and camera-based traffic analytics, and heat maps of dwell time.
segments.tr: Toko mengukurnya: penghitung pintu, analitik lalu lintas berbasis Wi-Fi dan kamera, dan peta panas waktu tinggal.

segments.src: The scoreboard metrics are simple enough to write in plain text:
segments.tr: Metrik papan skor cukup sederhana untuk ditulis dalam teks biasa:

segments.src: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area
segments.tr: sales per square foot = annual sales / selling area

segments.src: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors
segments.tr: conversion rate = transactions / store visitors

segments.src: average transaction value = sales / transactions
segments.tr: average transaction value = sales / transactions

segments.src: Layout and VMD are levers on all three.
segments.tr: Tata letak dan VMD adalah tuas di ketiga-tiganya.
